findings.message: This uses the nullish coalescing operator (`??`), but the toolchain is pinned to `@babel/preset-env` ^7.2.3 and `babel-eslint`. preset-env only transforms `??` from 7.8 on, and old babel-eslint can't parse it. On a lockfile or install that resolves to an older version, the build or lint can fail, or untranspiled `??` can end up in the dist bundle that rollup targets at IE11. Either confirm the minimum versions or use `options.timeout != null ? options.timeout : Infinity`.

`timeout` is never validated. A non-numeric value breaks the check silently: a string like '100' makes `Date.now() + '100'` a concatenated string that parses to a huge number, so the timeout never fires. NaN makes `Date.now() <= NaN` false, so the sync loop never runs and the call returns undefined right away. Convert with Number() and check that the result is finite, or ignore invalid values.

The deadline is only checked between edit lengths. One `execEditLength()` call walks every diagonal and runs `extractCommon` on each, which can take a long time on large inputs, so the real running time can go well past `timeout`. Say this in the docs, or also check the time inside the diagonal loop.

The new `timeout` option isn't in the README options list next to `maxEditLength`. Nothing tells users that a timeout makes the call return `undefined` (sync) or call the callback with no arguments (async). Nothing in the change tests the new code path either.
